close_reason: Added item 3 of the crate-level 'Spec-driven divergences (deliberate, do not fix)' rustdoc section documenting serde_json::{Map,Value} in the public API surface as a deliberate workspace-policy trade-off. The README Gotchas section and PLAN.md Extras-preservation section already cover the policy; this is the third surface (cargo doc landing page) making the trade-off discoverable. Lock-in to serde_json's major version is the explicit and accepted cost of the workspace extras-preservation policy — a future PR proposing to 'decouple from serde_json' would have to back out the workspace-wide policy first.
description:
**Contract risk**: every public struct in this crate carries

    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>

per workspace extras-preservation policy, and `AlertTrigger::Unknown`
holds a `serde_json::Value` directly. `serde_json::Map` and
`serde_json::Value` are therefore part of the public API surface.

**What goes wrong for callers**:
- If `serde_json` cuts a major version, this crate must major-bump
  in lockstep, because consumers using `link.extra.get(...)` would
  see breaking changes in `serde_json::Map`'s methods. The
  workspace cannot decouple from serde_json's release cadence.
- A consumer that wants to operate on the extras programmatically
  (e.g. validate that a particular vendor key is present) must
  import `serde_json` and pin to whatever version this crate uses.
  Multi-version mismatches are a real possibility — e.g. consumer
  on serde_json 2.x but this crate on 1.x.
- The same applies to `AlertTrigger::Unknown(v)` — pattern-matching
  on this variant forces consumers into `serde_json::Value` ergonomics
  (`.get(...)`, `.as_str()`, etc.).

**Defended? Partly**: README §"How it works" notes the choice;
PLAN.md §"Extras-preservation policy" rationalizes it. Workspace
AGENTS.md mandates the pattern. So the maintainer has chosen to
accept this risk crate-family-wide. But: the README does not warn
consumers that serde_json is part of the public-API surface they
inherit.

**Fix shape** (workspace-architectural, not crate-local):
Option 1: stay as-is, document in README that `serde_json` is a
public-API dep and a serde_json major bump forces a jmap-* major bump.
Option 2: introduce a workspace-owned `JmapExtras` newtype wrapping
`serde_json::Map` to insulate consumers from serde_json's API. Costs
maintenance, gains independence.

Label as `opinion` if the workspace-wide accepted-risk reading holds;
file in the visible queue so future PRs that propose changing
serde_json majors have a thread to land on.
title: serde_json::{Map,Value} appears in the public API surface via the extras field on every struct and AlertTrigger::Unknown — locks the major version of serde_json into the crate's contract
